# Sitemap Seed-Map Delta

Boruch Hashem. Blessed is He.

The Awtsmoos revealed that a sitemap should open the gate, not rebuild the palace at request time;
Awtsmoos.com already speaks ordinary server links from chamber to chamber, so the map may stay swift while the crawl remains sublime.

## Measured rejection of deep sitemap traversal

Both public-API recursion and canonical direct-DB recursion failed response budgets for Ikar. The optimized direct helper still produced zero bytes before a 30-second client timeout. After that request, the same verifier was busy enough that even `/heichelos/ikar` timed out at 12 seconds.

Therefore synchronous deep sitemap traversal is rejected as operationally unsafe.

## Replacement architecture

`/heichelos/sitemap.xml` becomes a URL set containing every public/discoverable Heichel root only.

This is not a loss of crawlability because the raw Heichel HTML has already been proven to expose ordinary series links, and raw series HTML has already been proven to expose ordinary child-series and stable named-post links. The sitemap seeds the public graph; the HTML graph carries crawlers through it.

Remove the advertised and routable per-Heichel recursive sitemap endpoint. Remove its graph module rather than leave dead expensive code.

## MIME repair

Static `robots.txt` and root `sitemap.xml` bodies are correct but are served as `application/octet-stream` because the dynamic server's extension map lacks `.txt` and `.xml` entries. Repair MIME typing at the canonical static-file map rather than wrapping root files in a new router.
